components.name: Cluster Chain
components.description: The live request path: dashed outside nodes, solid home nodes, the arrival node in signal, flowing connectors.
components.css: .ds-band { background: #211f1d; color: #f6f3ec; padding: 24px; font-family: 'Public Sans Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-chain { display: flex; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; } .ds-chain li { position: relative; flex: 1 1 0; padding: 0.85rem 0.9rem; border: 1.5px dashed #9c5a3c; border-radius: 0.5rem; font-weight: 650; line-height: 1.25; text-align: center; } .ds-chain li + li { margin-left: 2rem; } .ds-chain li + li::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 50%; right: 100%; width: 2rem; height: 2px; margin-right: 1.5px; background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, #e8693a 0 6px, transparent 6px 12px); background-size: 12px 2px; animation: ds-flow 1600ms linear infinite; } .ds-chain li.home { border-style: solid; border-color: #e8693a; background: #3a3530; } .ds-chain li.arrive { background: #e8693a; border-color: #e8693a; color: #1c1917; } @keyframes ds-flow { to { background-position: 12px 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-chain li + li::before { animation: none; } }

components.css: .ds-paper { background: #f6f3ec; color: #292524; padding: 24px 64px 24px 24px; font-family: 'Public Sans Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-record { display: block; width: 12rem; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; } .ds-rec { position: relative; aspect-ratio: 1; --sleeve: #211f1d; } .ds-sleeve { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--sleeve); outline: 1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.1); outline-offset: -1px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(20 14 8 / 0.3), 0 12px 24px -12px rgb(20 14 8 / 0.55); } .ds-disc { position: absolute; inset: 3%; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle, #1c1917 0 2.5%, #e8693a 3% 17%, transparent 17.5%), repeating-radial-gradient(circle, #33302d 0 2px, #1a1817 2px 4px); outline: 1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.3); translate: 11% 0; transition: translate 500ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-record:hover .ds-disc, .ds-record:focus-visible .ds-disc { translate: 19% 0; } .ds-cap { display: grid; gap: 0.1rem; margin: 0.9rem 0 0; } .ds-cap strong { font-size: 1.125rem; line-height: 1.3; } .ds-cap span { color: #57534e; } .ds-record:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
The site reads like a well-kept engineering record printed on warm paper and bound between charcoal covers. Charcoal bands open the page (hero), carry the infrastructure story (the cluster), and close it (contact). In between, warm paper holds the record itself: the work, the research, education and skills, each a dated entry separated by plain rules. Then one ember orange signal marks what is live or actionable: the main action, the moment you hover or focus, the last hop of the request that served this page.

The tone is calm and confident. Nothing is decorated for its own sake. Type does the work: one variable sans set very heavy and tight at display sizes, and relaxed and readable at body sizes. Imagery is real: product screenshots, a portrait, photos of the actual gear and records. Placeholders admit they are placeholders.

Density is moderate. The page is long and single-column on phones. On wide screens it opens into a two-column grid with a sticky left rail for section titles, so a hiring visitor can scan it in about a minute.
keyCharacteristics: Three surfaces only: charcoal band, warm paper, and the ember signal.
One typeface (Public Sans Variable), with weight and tracking setting the hierarchy.
Flat surfaces separated by rules. Only physical objects (screenshots, record sleeves) cast shadows.
Pill-shaped actions, gently rounded objects, square text structure.
Motion is small and physical: things lift, discs slide, the live path flows.

rules.name: The One Ember Rule
rules.body: The signal is the only saturated colour on the page. It marks the main action, interaction states, and live things. It never fills a section, a card or a heading.

rules.name: The Quiet Hover Rule
rules.body: Hover always raises contrast, never lowers it. On the charcoal band, buttons hover to cream (on-band fill, charcoal-band text). Text links on the band keep their cream text and gain a 2px signal underline; orange text on charcoal is lower contrast than cream. The Contact pill is the one signal fill, since its dark text on the signal stays above 5:1.

rules.name: The Raised Band Rule
rules.body: In dark mode the band is lighter than the ground (#2a2724 over #131211), never darker. A band must always read as a separate surface.

rules.name: The Weight Ladder Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from weight and size, never from colour or uppercase: 800 for titles, 650 to 700 for entries, labels and actions, 400 for reading.

rules.name: The Pretty Wrap Rule
rules.body: Headings use text-wrap: balance; leads and bullets use text-wrap: pretty. Never ship a one-word last line in a heading.

rules.name: The Ladder Rule
rules.body: New spacing takes a step from the scale. If no step fits, the layout is wrong, not the scale.

rules.name: The Heading Leads Rule
rules.body: There is always more space above a heading than below it, so the heading belongs to what follows it.

rules.name: The Objects Lift Rule
rules.body: Only real objects get shadows. Text blocks, entries, nav, and sections never do. If something new isn't a picture of a thing, it stays flat.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted toward umber (rgb(20 14 8 / …)), never neutral grey or blue-black.

dos: Do keep the ember signal for the main action, interaction states and live things only (The One Ember Rule).
Do put text on the signal in on-signal umber, never white.
Do separate sections with the 2px ink rule inside the gutter, and entries with 1px paper-seam rules.
Do use real screenshots and photos, and the dashed slot when a photo is missing.
Do set every new heading in Public Sans Variable at 650 to 800 weight with negative tracking, and balance its wrap.
Do tint shadows warm and give them only to objects (The Objects Lift Rule).
Do use the shared ease-out curve (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)), and turn off every transition and animation under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do give every focusable element a visible ring: currentColor on paper, the signal on the band.
Do keep every link and button at least 24×24px (WCAG 2.2, 2.5.8). Go links and nav links get there with vertical padding.

Do keep the first paint fast. On desktop the largest paint on load is the hero name, so the Public Sans latin file is preloaded. On phones it is the portrait, which carries fetchpriority="high". Anything new above the fold must not push either back.

Do glue a short last word to the one before it with a non-breaking space (this page. in the hero summary), so no paragraph ends on one stranded word. Keep curly quotes, real dashes and the ellipsis character in copy.
Do check print (or Save as PDF) after layout changes: light palette, link addresses visible, nothing split across pages.

Do keep page scripts as separate files. nginx sends a Content-Security-Policy that blocks inline scripts, so astro.config.mjs sets Vite's assetsInlineLimit to 0. A script that works in dev but not in production is probably being inlined.
donts: Don't add a second accent colour, gradients, or coloured section backgrounds beyond the charcoal band.
Don't use cards, boxed entries or shadows for text content.
Don't add a second typeface. Monospace is only for code and hashes.
Don't use uppercase labels or letter-spaced eyebrows. Hierarchy comes from weight.
Don't make the dark-mode band darker than the ground.
Don't invent metrics, logos or testimonials to fill space. Use a visible placeholder instead.
